report.source_text: After surgery, the patient showed persistent normalization of physical and serological parameters and full recovery of her renal function. She did not have any medical or surgical postoperative complication. At 10 months follow-up, she was in good general conditions, without signs of local recurrence, with a regular GI function and no signs of renal insufficiency or electrolyte disturbance.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 75-year-old woman with chronic renal insufficiency presented with persistent mucous diarrhea, vomiting, confusion, epigastric pain, and weight loss. Digital rectal examination identified a large circumferential rectal lesion. Colonoscopy revealed a giant rectal polyp (8-9 cm, occupying three quarters of the circumference). Biopsy confirmed a villous adenoma with focal high-grade dysplasia. Laboratory tests on admission demonstrated hyponatremia, hypokalemia, elevated creatinine and blood urea nitrogen consistent with renal impairment from severe dehydration linked to secretory diarrhea. Abdominal examination was nontender. CT scan excluded local invasion and metastases. Initial management with intravenous fluids and PPI infusion led to normalization of biochemistry and renal function over 10 days. Intraoperative frozen section revealed intramucosal adenocarcinoma requiring abdomino-perineal resection with end-colostomy. Postoperative course was uneventful with full recovery of renal function and no electrolyte disturbances at 10 months follow-up, consistent with resolution of McKittrick-Wheelock syndrome.
